The core insight is that pitch classification relies on modeling the kinematic space of pitches through multivariate statistics. Each pitch type corresponds to a distinct region in a high-dimensional feature space defined by velocity, spin rate, and movement parameters. The method assumes that these features are sufficient to separate pitch types, enabling probabilistic assignment via Gaussian mixture models. The failure mode arises when pitch kinematics are indistinguishable or when sample sizes are too small for reliable estimation. Dualities emerge between pitcher roles (starter vs. relief) and pitch repertoire, which must be encoded into priors or learned through hierarchical modeling. The model's robustness depends on accurate feature extraction from PITCHf/x data and appropriate regularization to avoid overfitting.
